Commentary: Jan Balt to Jason Smith, THATS OUT!! Bowled!!

Jan Balt to Jason Smith, out Bowled!! Balt has his man and South Africa have lost both set batters. Was nicely tossed up from round the wicket and drifted across the right-hander - Smith was down on his knee as he went for a big slog-sweep, missed the angle completely and has his off-stump clattered. Can Namibia keep South Africa to under 330? Jason Smith b Jan Balt 18(21) [4s-1]

Jack Brassell to Nqobani Mokoena, SIX, just over long-off, hard length outside off and Mokoena swung through the line - plenty of height and it has enough to clear the back leaping fielder at long-off

Jack Brassell to Nqobani Mokoena, byes, 2 runs, a comedy of errors, but South Africa get two byes and finish with 335 on the board. On a length and just outside off - Mokoena swung across the line and missed. They were always running for the bye, but Nqabayomzi Peter had given up as Zane Green shied and missed at the striker's end. Brassell collected with Mokoena stranded out in the middle, rolls the ball towards the stumps and misses once again. It runs away to long-on and they collect an additional run

13:12 Local Time, 11:12 GMT, 16:42 IST: A much better effort with the ball from Namibia, but they've still conceded a pile of runs. If Jordan Hermann scored a maiden ODI hundred the other day, today it was Connor Esterhuizen's turn. He was well supported by Tony de Zorzi and the pair added 183 runs for the second wicket. This partnership was followed by a few cameos, allowing the visitors to cruise past the 300-run mark. Namibia did come back well in the last few overs, but the damage had been done by then. Four wickets for the young Jack Brassell while Ruben Trumpelmann and Jan Balt took two each. Can Namibia chase down 335 and keep the series alive? Back shortly for the chase..
